articles.summary: Key Takeaways Hair type is more than curl pattern. Texture, density, porosity, strand thickness, and scalp health all influence how your hair behaves. Every hair type has a unique structure. Straight, wavy, curly, and coily hair each have different moisture, styling, and maintenance needs. Porosity affects moisture movement. Hair's ability to absorb and retain moisture plays a major role in dryness, frizz, and product performance. Scalp health influences hair health. Oil production, moisture balance, and scalp condition help shape how your hair looks and feels. The best routine is personalized. Understanding your hair's unique architecture helps you choose products and techniques that support healthier-looking hair.
articles.title: Hair Type Guide: How to Identify Your Hair Type, Porosity, Density, and Scalp Needs

articles.summary: The Ingredient of the Month series highlights one of our meticulously-selected ingredients. Get to know them all on our newly-launched Ingredients Page. Welcome back to another installment of Ingredient of the Month. This time around we’re highlighting one of our most beloved ingredients — rose extract. Found in multiple best-selling Function of Beauty formulas, rose extract offers an array of notable benefits for the hair that you should know about. Here, everything you need to know about rose extract. Main benefits: Delivers moisture to the hair, helps prevent split ends, balances excess oil + flakes GOALS: fix split ends hair goal for custom hair serum + custom leave-in Widely renowned for its highly therapeutic benefits, rose extract is a time-tested ingredient commonly used in a variety of personal care products — from serums and moisturizers, to shampoo and conditioner. Rich in vitamins A, C, D, and E, as well as essential fatty acids, rose extract is a powerful antioxidant with both soothing and hydrating properties. Moreover, it can help balance oil on the face or scalp. When it comes to the hair, specifically, rose extract aids in preventing split ends, delivering deep moisture to dry frizzy strands, and keeping oil under control. Rose extract also has a stunning floral scent profile, which makes it an excellent ingredient to use in natural fragrances. Currently, you can find rose extract in our hair serum and leave-in formulas. It’s worth noting that we use a synthetic form of rose because, believe it or not, producing a single pound of rose essential oil can take roughly 10,000 pounds of rose petals. Pretty wild, right? That’s why we went the synthetic route, to help sustain our Earth’s natural resources.
articles.title: Ingredient of the Month: Rose Extract

articles.summary: Meet Hien Kaplan — one of our amazing three co-founders here at Function of Beauty. Hien is a fearless leader, a super-brilliant formulation scientist, and an awesome mom to boot. Ahead, learn more about Hien, her background, and why she's so proud to be part of the Asian American Pacific Islander (AAPI) community. Full name: Hien Nguyen Kaplan Ethnicity: Vietnamese Occupation: Formulation scientist + co-founder of Function of Beauty Family:Hien is one of eight sisters and four brothers Earliest beauty memory: Watching her sister make a toner for her skin out of rice water Beauty role model: Her mom, who grew her own plants, showing her the importance of hard work and the power of plants Hair type + goals: Wavy, shine + anti-frizz Favorite scent: Eucalyptus Why she's proud to be part of the AAPI community: "Because we're all unique and special and have our own stories to tell." Her experience in the AAPI community: "I came from a really big family, coming to America. We all have a place here and we all matter; we all have something to bring and that should be recognized." Done reading? Keep up with Hien on Instagram @functionofhien!
articles.title: Get To Know: Function of Beauty Co-Founder Hien Kaplan
